estimatedFields: the docking time: the Russian mission-control report and RussianSpaceWeb give 09:21:40 UTC, used here; Wikipedia, Spacefacts and Weebau give 09:21:03. No source says whether the two are contact and capture
the end of the hover: mission control has the craft at 130 m by 09:13:40, so it is drawn ending 8 min before the docking; the approach from 80 m (09:14:50) to contact is not documented
the latching after contact (8 min) and the frames' 0.3 m gap at capture
the path from behind and below to the hover point, the closing speed and every camera move
the docking unit's frame, cone and the engines' place on Zvezda's aft end
the altitude: 379 x 388 km (Orbital Focus), drawn at 384 km
PMA-2 and PMA-3 as they sat that day: drawn on Unity's forward and nadir ports

provenance.l: Russian mission control (ISSCOM.002, 2 November 2000): hovering commenced at 150 m from the docking port at 09:12:12 UTC; 130 m at 0.4 m/s 09:13:40, 100 m at 0.7 m/s 09:14:16, 80 m at 0.4 m/s 09:14:50; docking 09.21.40 UTC
RussianSpaceWeb (Zak): launch 10:52:47.241 Moscow time on 31 October 2000; docking at Zvezda's aft port 12:21:40 Moscow time (actual), 12:24 planned; automatic Kurs approach
Spacefacts: launch 31 October 2000, 07:52:47 UTC; docking 2 November 2000, 09:21:03 UTC
Wikipedia: docking 2 November 2000, 09:21:03 UTC, Zvezda aft

Orbital Focus, Expedition 1 diary: the station's orbit 379 x 388 km, 51.6 degrees; PMA-3 on the lower face of Unity; Progress M1-3 undocking before the crew came and Progress M1-4 docking later, at Zarya's nadir port; P6 added afterwards
Wikipedia: Progress M1-3 undocked from Zvezda's aft port on 1 November 2000
Wikipedia: STS-92 installed the Z1 truss on Unity's zenith port and PMA-3 on its nadir port in October 2000
Wikipedia: the SSVP probe-and-drogue docking system, its 800 mm transfer tunnel
Weebau: Zvezda's aft transfer chamber, 2.0 m across and 2.34 m long
